title: Orchestrator for multi-region dedicated fleets: placement strategies, graceful failover, and data-residency enforcement
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and implement an orchestration component that places Dedicated fleet capacity across multiple regions and availability zones while honoring per-customer data residency constraints and throughput SLAs. This work ties together placement rules, autoscaling policies, traffic fencing for residency, and a graceful cross-zone/region failover mechanism so customer workloads maintain throughput guarantees during zone failures or planned maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: Placement engine exposes a placement policy API supporting: explicit region list, soft-preferred regions, zone anti-affinity, and residency-only constraints (e.g., EU-only)
Autoscaler can scale a regional fleet independently but respects global throughput guarantees configured per-customer (capacity reservations and burst buckets)

Failover behaviour: when an active zone reports degraded health, traffic is rerouted to in-region fallback zones; only when no in-region capacity is available does cross-region failover occur and only for customers without residency restrictions
Data residency enforcement: control-plane rejects cross-region scheduling for customers with residency flag; audit logs record all placement decisions and rejected actions
End-to-end tests validate throughput SLO during simulated zone outages with <=10% variance from normal for non-residency customers when cross-region failover is allowed
Console UI surfaces per-fleet residency, placement policy, and per-region capacity utilization; API returns placement traces for troubleshooting
implementation_notes: Introduce a PlacementService module in fleet-orchestrator responsible for decision logic; keep API idempotent and queryable
Leverage existing Heartbeat/NodeIndex for zone health; add a region-level health aggregator to avoid noisy failovers
Extend autoscaler to accept placement hints and a ‘placement-strategy’ param (strict | preferred | best_effort)
Represent residency as an immutable customer property at provisioning time; propagate to all scheduling decisions
Add a cross-region capacity pool model for non-residency customers to allow controlled bursts; tracked separately for billing and telemetry
Emit detailed audit events (placement.request, placement.decision, placement.reject, failover.trigger, failover.completed) to EventBridge and Console
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design doc + API schema + security review (placement API, residency flags, audit schema)
Week 2: Implement PlacementService prototypes and unit tests (local simulated node sets)
Week 3: Integrate placement hints into autoscaler and add region health aggregator; add migration script for existing fleets
Week 4: End-to-end staging rollout with synthetic traffic, simulate AZ and region outages, iterate on failover thresholds
Week 5: Console and API surface updates, update docs, run compliance audit for residency enforcement
Week 6: Canary: enable for small set of customers (opt-in), monitor metrics, prepare runbook and rollback steps
testing_plan: Unit tests for placement decision matrix (rules + residency)
Integration tests with autoscaler that validate scale-up/scale-down while preserving reserved throughput
Chaos testing in staging: kill zone controllers, network partitions between region control planes, and simulate node flapping
Throughput SLO tests: run 1k QPS workload across fleets with and without cross-region failover; measure tail latency and effective tokens/sec
Security tests: verify residency flag cannot be changed post-provision without proper audit and admin approval
Regression: ensure existing Dedicated APIs remain backward-compatible (no breaking schema changes)
rollout_plan: Feature-flag entire PlacementService; default behavior unchanged for existing fleets
Enable for internal test orgs and a small subset of paid customers: gather telemetry for 2 weeks
Open opt-in to more customers while monitoring failover metrics and billing reconciliation
Gradually flip default for new Dedicated fleet creations to use new placement policies; existing fleets require opt-in or migration tool
Publish runbook for on-call to handle cross-region failover incidents and manual overrides
metrics_and_alerting: Failover frequency and duration per region — alert on >2 failovers/hour for a region
Cross-region failover rate for residency-constrained customers (should be 0) — alert on any occurrence
Throughput SLO breach rate during failovers — tracked in Console and sent to SLO dashboard
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Noisy health signals cause frequent failovers => Mitigation: region-level aggregation + debounce window + leader election for failover orchestration
Risk: Billing mismatch when cross-region burst capacity used => Mitigation: separate metering for cross-region pool and pre-flight capacity checks with customer notification
Risk: Residency flag misconfiguration leads to compliance exposure => Mitigation: enforce immutability, admin approval flow, automated audits
Risk: Autoscaler thrashes when placement constrains available nodes => Mitigation: integrate placement-aware cooldowns and reservations
docs_and_followups: Playbook: Failover handling and manual override steps (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/playbooks/failover-dedicated)
Post-mortem template to capture any customer-impacting failovers during rollout
Follow-up ticket: ENG-4805 — UI for bulk migration of existing fleets to new placement model
